title: Passenger Portal — sign on to an anonymous account
preface: This test is to confirm that a customer can sign on to the Passenger Web Portal with a card that has journeys in the previous seven days.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the Passenger Web Portal sign-on page is displayed
**AND** the customer's payment card or mobile wallet has completed journeys in the previous seven days (**UNCONFIRMED** — no source found tying sign-on eligibility itself to a 7-day recency window; PSPEC-0015 Fig.51 confirms a 7-calendar-day *view* window for an anonymous account's history but not a sign-on precondition — gap Q26)

steps.content: **WHEN** the customer enters valid card details
steps.expected:
**THEN** the customer is signed on to their anonymous account
**AND** the account home screen is displayed

change_note: Terse-mandate: no body change needed beyond the UNCONFIRMED marker. Added Refs. Flagged the '7 days to sign on' claim as unconfirmed — PSPEC-0015 describes anonymous cEMV login as card-details entry only (§6.1.1.1), and the only '7 days' figure found (Fig.51 footnote *) governs the anonymous account's Journey/Transaction History view window post-sign-on, not sign-on eligibility. Logged gap Q26; do not silently keep or silently change the precondition until answered.

title: Account Functions — view and print Journey History
preface: This test is to confirm that a customer can view and print the Journey History for their payment card or mobile wallet in the Passenger Web Portal.
preconds: **GIVEN** a customer is signed on to the Passenger Web Portal and the account home screen is displayed

steps.expected:
**THEN** the journeys for the card or mobile wallet are listed
**AND** the journey history can be printed

change_note: RESOLVED the flagged print-vs-download question: 'print' is CORRECT, not George's suspected 'download'. PSPEC-0015 (CloudFare ABT Product Specification v4.2.1) Figure 51 'web/mobile app portal functionality for customer' explicitly lists the feature as 'View (and print) Journey History' for both Anonymous and Registered accounts. No wording change needed — only citation added (case had no Refs at all before). Note: the Laval user-portal manual (a different deployment) was correctly excluded per the task brief; PSPEC-0015 is the base CloudFare ABT product spec underlying the Translink build, filed alongside the Translink Cloudfare manual in the same requirements library, and is not contradicted by anything Translink-specific found. A separate, distinct 'download in Excel/CSV' feature also exists in PSPEC-0015 (para 15374) for Transaction data specifically, for expense purposes — that is an additional feature, not a replacement of 'print', and is not currently claimed by any case in this section.

title: Account Functions — request a refund
preface: This test is to confirm that a customer can raise a refund request for a transaction on their account from the Passenger Web Portal.
preconds: **GIVEN** a customer is signed on to the Passenger Web Portal and viewing their transaction history

steps.content: **WHEN** the customer raises a refund request for a transaction (via aftercare)
steps.expected: **THEN** the refund request is submitted for operator approval and second-operator authorisation

change_note: Grounded: PSPEC-0015 Fig.51 lists 'Submit refund request' under Helpdesk/Aftercare functions available via the customer portal. Citation added; no wording change. Note: the case's 'second-operator authorisation' detail was not separately found in PSPEC-0015's Fig.51 row (which only names the submit action, not the approval workflow depth) — left as-is per no-gap-filling (not invented by us, was already live text) but flagged in the changelog as a softer, unresolved sourcing point, not elevated to a blocking GAP since a refund-approval-workflow claim is plausible and not contradicted anywhere found.

title: Account Functions — retry a declined payment
preface: This test is to confirm that a customer can retry a declined payment from the Passenger Web Portal (web-initiated re-authorisation), clearing the outstanding amount on success.
preconds: **GIVEN** a customer is signed on to the Passenger Web Portal with a declined payment on their account (card on the deny list)

steps.expected:
**THEN** a web-initiated re-authorisation is attempted
**AND** on a successful retry the outstanding amount is cleared and the card is removed from the deny list

refs: PSPEC-0015 §4.9.3 Customer Online Debt Recovery,PSPEC-0015 Fig.51 (Pay outstanding EMV debt)
change_note: Grounded: PSPEC-0015 §4.9.3 'Customer Online Debt Recovery' describes exactly this — the customer accesses their account, is notified the card is on the deny list, selects the declined transaction to instigate a new authorisation request; a successful retry removes them from the deny list. Fig.51 also lists 'Pay outstanding EMV debt (online debt recovery)'. Citation added; no wording change needed — case was already accurate.

title: Metro cap — a declined journey is not treated as a settled capped tap
preface: This test is to confirm that a declined Metro journey is not wrongly treated as a settled capped tap when an alighting-stop correction is attempted on it.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded ABT test cEMV card on the Translink test account (CloudFare env5)
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal to view Journey History
**AND** the card has one Metro journey that was declined at the reader (e.g. the card in a deny-listed state, Declined Reason 2), shown in Journey History as declined
**AND** CR122 alighting-stop correction is available

steps.content:
**WHEN** you open the card's Journey History
**AND** you attempt to correct the alighting stop on the declined journey (**UNCONFIRMED** — whether a correction option is even exposed for a declined/deny-listed journey is not stated in FBD-100662 §5.6 or TODEV-24096; the spec describes the correction indicator for bus journeys generally, not declined-journey handling specifically — confirm on the live system, gap Q25)
steps.expected:
**THEN** the journey is still handled as declined
**AND** it is not treated as a settled capped journey
**AND** no cap charge is produced for it

change_note: Two fixes per George's flag: (1) reordered the WHEN — 'open Journey History' now comes before 'attempt the correction' (was backwards/compound: you can't attempt a portal action on a journey without first having it open). (2) The underlying premise (can you even attempt a CR122 correction on a DECLINED journey at all) is not confirmed by FBD-100662 §5.6 (paras 691-694, read in full) or by anything else in the requirements library — the spec discusses the correction indicator appearing on 'all bus journeys' but never distinguishes declined/deny-listed journeys from settled ones. Rather than invent that the option either is or isn't offered, marked the attempt itself UNCONFIRMED and logged gap Q26->Q25 (see gap-register). The expected OUTCOME (still declined, not treated as capped, no charge) is left as the correct assertion either way — if the correction option turns out not to be offered at all for declined journeys, this case's real behaviour to test would be 'no correction option is shown', which the gap answer will clarify. Swept all 33 sibling cases in the same CR122 capping batch (C4102757-4102790 excl. C4102766) for the same 'mechanical CR122 stamp' risk per George's request: every one of them genuinely attempts or holds a CR122 alighting-stop correction on a settled (including £0.00-capped) journey, so the CR122 precondition is relevant in all 33 — no further fix needed there.
